gaps.sentence: By next April, we ___ here for ten years.
gaps.hint: duration leading up to a future point
gaps.explanation: A duration leading up to a future point takes the future perfect continuous: will have been living.

gaps.sentence: Look — someone ___ that vase; it is in pieces on the floor.
gaps.hint: look plus a visible present result
gaps.explanation: The present result of a very recent action takes the present perfect: has broken.

gaps.sentence: It is the first time I ___ paella.
gaps.hint: it is the first time takes present perfect
gaps.explanation: After 'It is the first time', English uses the present perfect: have eaten.

gaps.sentence: Don't wake him — he has just ___ asleep.
gaps.explanation: 'Has just' is followed by the past participle: fallen.

gaps.sentence: Don't disturb him — he ___ an important video call with the client.
gaps.hint: do not disturb means it is happening now
gaps.explanation: An action in progress at the moment of speaking takes the present continuous: is having.

gaps.sentence: This time next week I ___ across the desert.
gaps.hint: action in progress at a future time
gaps.explanation: 'This time next week' — future continuous for an ongoing future action.

gaps.sentence: She is exhausted because she ___ since dawn.
gaps.hint: since dawn explains her present exhaustion
gaps.explanation: An action running from the past to now and explaining a present state takes the present perfect continuous: has been travelling.

gaps.sentence: We ___ each other since primary school.
gaps.explanation: 'Since primary school' — present perfect of a state verb.
